resources.string: The mobile contract and cryptographic services have been checked.
This build cannot use the cryptographic core. Install a valid operational build.
Verification build: the interface and system pickers work, but cryptographic operations are disabled.

1. Select a document in Android or share it with GrxFirma.

2. To sign, import a protected PKCS#12 file or tap “DNIe over NFC”. For NFC, enter the six CAN digits printed on the DNIe and hold the card against the back of the phone. The SIGNATURE certificate is used and the PIN is requested when signing. The private key stays on the card.

3. Choose automatic, PAdES, CAdES or XAdES format and confirm signing. Save the result with the Android picker. Tap “Forget certificate” when finished.

4. Verification reports cryptographic integrity, certificate validity, chain trust and revocation availability separately. Without Internet access, it can only consider revocation evidence embedded in the signature.

The screen accepts one document per operation. Screenshots are blocked in the production build.
Select the document you want to sign or verify.
To verify a detached signature such as CAdES, also select the original document. Leave this empty for signatures that already contain the document.
Choose a PKCS#12 file or use your DNIe over NFC. The DNIe key stays on the card.
Select the document you want to sign first.
Enter the six CAN digits printed on the front of the DNIe, at the bottom right.
The CAN must contain exactly six digits.
Hold the DNIe against the back of the phone until reading finishes.
The DNIe SIGNATURE certificate is ready. Choose a format and tap Sign; you will be asked for the PIN.
The NFC session ended when you left this screen. Hold the DNIe near the phone again to sign.
Keep the DNIe against the phone. Enter the PIN to sign this document.
This phone has no NFC. Use a PKCS#12 certificate or another compatible phone.
Turn on NFC in your phone settings and try again.
The DNIe could not be opened with that CAN. Check the six digits and hold the card near the phone again.
Incorrect PIN. Attempts remaining: %1$d. Check it before trying again.
Incorrect PIN. The remaining attempts could not be checked; verify the PIN before trying again.
The DNIe is blocked. Do not try again; visit a DNIe update point.
Connection to the DNIe was lost. Keep it against the phone and tap DNIe over NFC to retry.
The DNIe SIGNATURE certificate has expired. Renew the DNIe before signing.
No usable SIGNATURE certificate was found on this DNIe.
DNIe reading could not start in this installation. Update the app.
The DNIe could not be read or used. Keep the card against the phone and try again.
The password is used during import and is not stored persistently.
Drag the seal, resize it from the corner, or rotate it with the handle. You can also use the buttons.

The certificate is not currently valid. Use a valid certificate; renew it if it has expired.
The certificate or its key is not suitable for signing on Android. Use a signing certificate with RSA of at least 2048 bits or ECDSA of at least 256 bits.
The operation failed. Review your selection and try again.
This document contains signatures. Use co-signing
T and higher require a TSA. LT/LTA also check certificate revocation. B with a TSA produces T.
Enable the TSA and enter an HTTP or HTTPS URL without credentials or a fragment.
Unavailable combination: PAdES supports sign/co-sign and B/T/LT; XAdES supports B/T; CAdES supports B/T/LT/LTA and all three operations.
Signature created. Automatic verification failed; save it and verify it later.
The report was not saved. You can retry the export; the destination may contain a partial file.

First Android parity wave: co-signing and counter-signing; signature profiles and TSA; automatic and detailed verification; JSON report export; eleven languages and About.\n\nPAdES: B/T/LT and sign/co-sign. XAdES: B/T. CAdES: B/T/LT/LTA. Mobile verification checks integrity and embedded evidence; it does not establish trust using system anchors or check revocation online.
Cryptographic integrity checked; system chain trust has not been evaluated.
